claims.wording: The vendor describes four scanners: System Data, Duplicate Files, Large Files and Junk Files; duplicate matching uses SHA-256.
excerpts: Four categories: System Data (caches, logs, temporary files), Duplicate Files (exact matches via SHA-256), Large Files (forgotten exports, old simulators, VM files), and Junk Files (old installers plus leftover files from apps you've already uninstalled).
claims.conditions: Do not copy no-false-positives, complete coverage or safety guarantees.

claims.wording: DataSweeper documents handpicked removal to Trash and undo restoration from Trash.
excerpts: It scans everything, you handpick what you delete.
One click restores files from the Trash back to their original location.
claims.conditions: Undo is not evidence of recovery after emptying Trash. Moving files to Trash is not measured available-space recovery.

claims.wording: The homepage advertises $9.99 once with free future updates; the US App Store displays $9.99.
excerpts: $9.99 once. Free updates for life.
All future updates are completely free — no upgrade fees, no "pro" tiers, no expiring licenses.
Pay once, use forever.
claims.conditions: US storefront; no checkout performed. Other currencies, regional taxes, refund terms and future promises not independently verified. No DataSweeper app account claimed; Apple purchase/account requirements not tested. Refresh within 30 days and before publication.

excerpts: DataSweeper supports macOS Sequoia and macOS Tahoe. It runs natively on Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4) and Intel Macs.
Requires macOS 26.2 or later.
claims.conditions: Do not recommend Sequoia or assert current architecture coverage from homepage alone. Need consistent official version-specific requirements; no install attempted.

Version 1.0.8

claims.wording: DataSweeper's policy says operations stay local, with no network requests, tracking or app sign-in; it discloses Full Disk Access and Finder Automation requirements.
excerpts: No user accounts or sign-in are required.
No network requests are made by the Application. All file scanning and deletion operations are performed locally on your Mac.
The Application requires macOS Full Disk Access and Finder Automation permissions solely to scan files on your system and move items to the Trash via Finder.
claims.conditions: Attribute policy; do not claim independent privacy/security audit. Store purchase network access is not the same as app runtime behavior.

claims.wording: The homepage says DataSweeper scans only when opened and a scan is started; it disclaims a background agent, menu-bar daemon and scheduled processes.
excerpts: It only scans when you open it and start a scan. No background agent, no menu bar daemon, no scheduled processes running without your knowledge.
claims.conditions: App Store also advertises Siri Shortcuts automation and background scan notifications; those are not evidence of recurring growth monitoring, and do not necessarily contradict the absence of a persistent agent. Exact shortcuts behavior not tested.

workflow.title: Review Mac cleanup results before moving files to Trash
workflow.primaryIntent: Distinguish disposable caches, exact duplicate candidates and original work before accepting a scanner's suggestion.
workflow.keywordEvidence: Editorial hypotheses, not measured search volume or SERP research.
workflow.description: A scan result is a review list, not permission to delete. Separate caches, duplicate candidates and original work, then check the limits of Trash and undo.
outline: Lead: inspect purpose and ownership before size; affiliation at any Breathing Room recommendation
Top visual: permitted DataSweeper real UI after rights and actual visual review, not a generated interface
Separate system-data/cache candidates from originals and cloud-only items
Exact duplicate matching does not choose the right retained copy
Review path, app ownership, rebuild/download cost and backups before a Trash move
Trash, undo and permanent deletion are different states; do not promise space recovery
Later visual: labeled first-party Space example preview and limits
Choose an occasional scan versus a recurring investigation workflow
workflow.interactionPass: Propose a non-destructive three-question checklist: Is this original work? Can it be rebuilt/downloaded at acceptable cost? Is the owner/path and recovery plan understood? No filesystem access or deletion buttons.
workflow.length: 900–1400 words only if evidence earns it; no mandatory statistics/FAQ/code demo
workflow.distinctness: Focus on file-level review and reversibility, not a renamed product-vs-product matrix. Check other drafts for intent collision before reserving slug.
